sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《Hidden Brain》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: At the Olympic Games in 2021, one athlete arrived in Tokyo
sentences.zh: 在2021年奥运会上，一位运动员抵达东京时，

sentences.en: with a mountain of expectations on her four-foot, eight-inch frame.
sentences.zh: 她那四英尺八英寸的身躯上承载着如山的期望。

sentences.en: Five medals in Rio, four of them gold,
sentences.zh: 在里约奥运会上她拿下了五枚奖牌，其中四枚是金牌，

sentences.en: and could do even better than that this time around here in Tokyo.
sentences.zh: 而这一次在东京，人们认为她能做得更好。

sentences.en: If you don't think that that's hard, then you really don't understand gymnastics.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得这很容易，那你真的不懂体操。

sentences.en: People didn't just expect her to win gold medals in gymnastics.
sentences.zh: 人们对她的期待不仅仅是赢得体操金牌。

sentences.en: The expected magic.
sentences.zh: 人们期待的是奇迹。

sentences.en: I mean, she has just set herself so far apart from the rest of the field,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她已经让自己远远领先于其他选手了，

sentences.en: and not just on the competition floor.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是在赛场上。

sentences.en: Miles' pursuit of history starts tonight.
sentences.zh: 拜尔斯创造历史的征程今晚开启。

sentences.en: Four days into the Games, Simone Biles pulled out of the competition.
sentences.zh: 在奥运会开幕四天后，西蒙·拜尔斯退出了比赛。

sentences.en: I've just never felt like this going into a competition before,
sentences.zh: 我以前参加比赛时从未有过这种感觉，

sentences.en: and I tried to go out here and have fun and warm up in the back,
sentences.zh: 我试着上场享受比赛，在后台热身时，

sentences.en: went a little bit better, but then once I came out here, I was like,
sentences.zh: 感觉好了一些，但一旦来到这里，我就觉得，

sentences.en: no, mental is not there.
sentences.zh: 不行，我的心理状态不在那儿。

sentences.en: The world was stunned.
sentences.zh: 全世界都惊呆了。

sentences.en: An athlete with seemingly otherworldly powers was struggling.
sentences.zh: 一位拥有超凡能力的运动员竟然陷入了困境。

sentences.en: From the outside looking in, it seemed hard to understand.
sentences.zh: 从局外人的角度来看，这似乎很难理解。

sentences.en: And it raised a question.
sentences.zh: 这引发了一个问题。

sentences.en: If a world champion can be toppled by these emotions,
sentences.zh: 如果一位世界冠军都能被这些情绪击倒，

sentences.en: what does it mean for the rest of us?
sentences.zh: 那对我们其他人来说意味着什么？

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, the strange psychology of the voice inside our heads that says,
sentences.zh: 本周的《Hidden Brain》，我们将探讨脑海中那个声音的奇怪心理学，它会说：

sentences.en: the world may think you are amazing, but you are really just a fraud.
sentences.zh: 世界可能认为你很了不起，但你其实只是个骗子。

sentences.en: It's hard to see ourselves clearly.
sentences.zh: 看清自己很难。

sentences.en: This is true in all manner of situations,
sentences.zh: 这在各种情况下都是事实，

sentences.en: but it can be especially true when we are confronting a challenge.
sentences.zh: 但当我们面临挑战时，这一点尤其明显。

sentences.en: At such moments, many of us start to doubt ourselves.
sentences.zh: 在这样的时刻，我们许多人开始怀疑自己。

sentences.en: We think we are unequal to the task.
sentences.zh: 我们认为自己无法胜任这项任务。

sentences.en: At the University of Texas at Austin, Kevin Coakley researches the psychology of self-doubt.
sentences.zh: 在德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校，凯文·科克利研究自我怀疑的心理学。

sentences.en: He studies the corrosive effects these doubts can have on our well-being,
sentences.zh: 他研究这些怀疑对我们幸福感产生的腐蚀性影响，

sentences.en: but also how we might turn our internal misgivings into an ally.
sentences.zh: 同时也研究我们如何将内心的不安转化为盟友。

sentences.en: Kevin Coakley, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 凯文·科克利，欢迎来到《Hidden Brain》。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Kevin, you're a psychologist who studies the phenomenon of self-doubt,
sentences.zh: 凯文，你是一位研究自我怀疑现象的心理学家，

sentences.en: yet you yourself have not been immune to such doubts.
sentences.zh: 但你自己也未能幸免于这种怀疑。

sentences.en: I want to take you back to when you were 29 years old.
sentences.zh: 我想带你回到你29岁的时候。

sentences.en: You had just completed your PhD.
sentences.zh: 你刚刚完成了博士学位。

sentences.en: You had begun teaching.
sentences.zh: 你已经开始教书了。

sentences.en: Can you describe the fears that went through your mind as you prepared for class each day?
sentences.zh: 你能描述一下你每天备课时脑海中闪过的恐惧吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: I was a young assistant professor at Southern Illinois University at Carbondale.
sentences.zh: 那时我是南伊利诺伊大学卡本代尔分校的一名年轻助理教授。

sentences.en: And I can recall very vividly the feeling that I had walking the hallways of the psychology department there
sentences.zh: 我清楚地记得走在那里的心理学系走廊时的感觉，

sentences.en: and seeing on the walls these publications by my new colleagues, very accomplished colleagues.
sentences.zh: 看到墙上贴着我新同事们的出版物，他们都是非常有成就的同事。

sentences.en: And I had come out of graduate school with having only one publication.
sentences.zh: 而我从研究生院出来时只有一篇出版物。

sentences.en: I believe that I was hired on the basis that people saw potential in me, particularly in terms of my teaching.
sentences.zh: 我相信我被录用是因为人们看到了我的潜力，特别是在教学方面。

sentences.en: But I knew that I had a lot to prove in terms of research.
sentences.zh: 但我知道在研究方面我还有很多需要证明的地方。

sentences.en: And so when I was walking those hallways, I had this sense of, wow, like, can I do this?
sentences.zh: 所以当我走在那些走廊里时，我有一种感觉：哇，我能做到吗？

sentences.en: And it was incredibly stressful.
sentences.zh: 这压力太大了。

sentences.en: It sort of had me doubting whether, in fact, I belonged, whether I deserved to be there.
sentences.zh: 这让我怀疑自己是否真的属于那里，是否配得上那个位置。

sentences.en: And I was aware that I was one of only a few Black professors at the university.
sentences.zh: 而且我意识到我是大学里为数不多的黑人教授之一。

sentences.en: And so I did not want to do anything that would result in students seeing me or believing me to not be qualified to be the professor.
sentences.zh: 所以我不想做任何会导致学生认为我不够格担任教授的事情。

sentences.en: So I made sure that I wore sports coats and wore ties to class every day.
sentences.zh: 所以我确保每天穿运动外套和打领带去上课。

sentences.en: I had a briefcase that I bought because, in my mind, a professor carries a briefcase.
sentences.zh: 我买了一个公文包，因为在我看来，教授就该提着公文包。

sentences.en: And so I was really working hard to project an image of expertise and authority that I imagined professors needing to represent.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很努力地去展现一种专业和权威的形象，我觉得教授就该是这样。

sentences.en: I understand that one way your self-doubt manifested was that you were worried about misspeaking in class, saying something wrong.
sentences.zh: 我了解到你自我怀疑的一种表现是担心在课堂上说错话。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, when you imagine making a mistake like that, what was the worst-case scenario that ran through your head?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，当你想象犯那种错误时，你脑海中最糟糕的情况是什么？

sentences.en: Speaking in front of a large introductory class, psychology class, I thought, man, I cannot stand here and misspeak.
sentences.zh: 在大型心理学入门课上发言时，我想，天哪，我不能站在这里说错话。

sentences.en: I need to make sure that I'm conjugating my verbs correctly.
sentences.zh: 我必须确保我的动词变位正确。

sentences.en: I need to make sure that I'm enunciating every word exactly correctly.
sentences.zh: 我必须确保我说的每一个字都准确无误。

sentences.en: And so for me, the worst-case scenario would have been to be lecturing and to say something incorrectly,
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，最糟糕的情况就是在讲课时说错了什么，

sentences.en: and then to have my students questioning my authority and ability to be an effective professor.
sentences.zh: 然后让学生质疑我的权威和作为一名有效率的教授的能力。

sentences.en: And so for me, that was a worst-case scenario.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，那是噩梦般的场景。

sentences.en: You've been a professor for a while now.
sentences.zh: 你当教授已经有一段时间了。

sentences.en: You clearly know what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 你显然很清楚自己在做什么。

sentences.en: You have a lengthy publication record.
sentences.zh: 你有很长的出版记录。

sentences.en: Have your self-doubts gone away?
sentences.zh: 你的自我怀疑消失了吗？

sentences.en: You know, that's a good question.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是个好问题。

sentences.en: It depends on the day that you ask me the question.
sentences.zh: 这取决于你是在哪一天问我这个问题。

sentences.en: When I'm speaking to people and when people are introducing me and they're reading my accolades,
sentences.zh: 当我向人们演讲，或者当人们介绍我并宣读我的荣誉时，

sentences.en: on the one hand, I feel pretty good about what I've been able to accomplish.
sentences.zh: 一方面，我对自己的成就感到相当自豪。

sentences.en: But there are still some days when I find myself doubting whether I have the expertise to be able to speak in front of people.
sentences.zh: 但仍有一些日子，我会怀疑自己是否有足够的专业知识在众人面前发言。

sentences.en: And when I talk to my students about this, they find it amazing because they have Dr. Kevin Coakley on somewhat of an academic pedestal.
sentences.zh: 当我与学生谈论这件事时，他们觉得很不可思议，因为他们把凯文·科克利博士放在了某种学术神坛上。

sentences.en: And when I tell them that even Dr. Coakley sometimes still suffers, you know, and still wonders about, you know,
sentences.zh: 当我告诉他们，即使是科克利博士有时也会感到痛苦，你知道，还会怀疑，你知道，

sentences.en: my deservedness to be in the position that I'm in, they are surprised.
sentences.zh: 怀疑自己是否配得上现在的职位，他们会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: So I do still have those experiences.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实仍然会有那种经历。

sentences.en: So, Kevin, it looks like you yourself are a walking example of this phenomenon that you have studied for many years.
sentences.zh: 所以，凯文，看来你自己就是你研究多年的这种现象的活生生的例子。

sentences.en: In popular culture, it's called the imposter syndrome.
sentences.zh: 在流行文化中，这被称为“冒充者综合征”。

sentences.en: Now, you think that term is overly clinical.
sentences.zh: 你认为这个术语过于临床化了。

sentences.en: You prefer the term imposter phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 你更喜欢“冒充者现象”这个词。

sentences.en: Can you describe for me what the imposter phenomenon is?
sentences.zh: 你能为我描述一下什么是冒充者现象吗？

sentences.en: The imposter phenomenon is basically the sentiment that one is being intellectually fraudulent.
sentences.zh: 冒充者现象基本上是一种认为自己在智力上是欺诈者的感觉。

sentences.en: It's the idea that individuals who are very accomplished, very competent, very intelligent people,
sentences.zh: 这是一种想法，即那些非常有成就、非常有能力、非常聪明的人，

sentences.en: nevertheless feel like they are fooling people.
sentences.zh: 却仍然觉得自己在欺骗别人。

sentences.en: They believe that they are not nearly as smart and competent as their accomplishments would suggeSt.
sentences.zh: 他们认为自己并不像他们的成就所暗示的那样聪明和能干。

sentences.en: So we're going to talk about the factors that produce these kinds of self-doubt and what we can do about these misgivings.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要谈谈产生这种自我怀疑的因素，以及我们能对这些不安做些什么。

sentences.en: But I want to start by looking at the different dimensions of self-doubt,
sentences.zh: 但我首先想看看自我怀疑的不同维度，

sentences.en: because when you start to peel this onion, it turns out to be a really complex phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 因为当你开始剥开这层洋葱时，你会发现这是一个非常复杂的现象。

sentences.en: I want to play you a clip of the actress Viola Davis talking to the CBS program 60 Minutes.
sentences.zh: 我想播放一段女演员维奥拉·戴维斯接受CBS《60分钟》节目采访的片段。

sentences.en: I don't know if it's healthy or not.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这是否健康。

sentences.en: I'm just saying that it's something that I recognize in all the artists I've worked with.
sentences.zh: 我只是说，这是我在所有合作过的艺术家身上都能认出的东西。

sentences.en: It's in all of them.
sentences.zh: 他们所有人都有。

sentences.en: So I know the language of the artiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我了解艺术家的语言。

sentences.en: And the language of the artist is, someone's going to find me out.
sentences.zh: 艺术家的语言就是：有人会揭穿我。

sentences.en: I may not be as great as people think I am.
sentences.zh: 我可能没有人们想象的那么伟大。

sentences.en: I may not be as great as people think I am.
sentences.zh: 我可能没有人们想象的那么伟大。

sentences.en: So one dimension of self-doubt here is that you worry that others might have an inflated sense of how good you are,
sentences.zh: 所以这里自我怀疑的一个维度是，你担心别人可能对你的评价过高，

sentences.en: that you might not be able to live up to those expectations?
sentences.zh: 担心你可能无法达到那些期望？

sentences.en: Yeah, that is one of the hallmark traits of imposter feelings.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是冒充者心理的标志性特征之一。

sentences.en: When you have friends and colleagues telling you how great you are and saying all of these nice and wonderful things about you,
sentences.zh: 当你的朋友和同事告诉你你有多棒，并对你说所有这些美好而美妙的事情时，

sentences.en: you find yourself just wondering, you know, can I live up to these lofty expectations?
sentences.zh: 你会发现自己只是在想，你知道，我能达到这些崇高的期望吗？

sentences.en: And you can't help but sort of feel that I can't live up to that.
sentences.zh: 你忍不住会觉得我无法达到那种程度。

sentences.en: So when Viola Davis made those remarks, it really sort of represented some of the classic hallmark signs of imposterism.
sentences.zh: 所以当维奥拉·戴维斯发表这些言论时，它确实代表了一些冒充者心理的经典标志性迹象。

sentences.en: So I'm wondering if this might be especially acute for an actor, but I think all of us might experience some version of this.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇这对于演员来说是否特别强烈，但我认为我们所有人可能都会经历某种形式的这种感觉。

sentences.en: You know, when you're shooting a movie, they don't show the audience all the takes when someone flubbed a line or made a mistake.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你拍摄电影时，他们不会向观众展示所有NG的镜头，或者某人说错台词或犯错的时候。

sentences.en: So Viola Davis thinks that we, the audience, associate her with the perfection of the role she's playing on the screen, what we see on the screen.
sentences.zh: 所以维奥拉·戴维斯认为我们观众将她与她在屏幕上扮演的角色所展现的完美联系在一起，也就是我们在屏幕上看到的。

sentences.en: She, on the other hand, knows the whole picture, all the mistakes, the off days, and she worries that our picture of her and her picture of her might not match.
sentences.zh: 而她自己则了解全貌，所有的错误、状态不佳的日子，她担心我们眼中的她和她眼中的她可能不匹配。

sentences.en: You are absolutely correct.
sentences.zh: 你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: What we see is the sort of perfected version of who she is as an actress.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的是她作为一名演员的完美版本。

sentences.en: What we don't see are, as you said, the many outtakes, you know, that I'm sure she's had to go through in order to get finally the perfect scene.
sentences.zh: 我们看不到的是，正如你所说，许多NG镜头，你知道，我相信她必须经历这些才能最终得到完美的场景。

sentences.en: Again, I mean, it's the idea that, you know,
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我的意思是，这是一种想法，你知道，

sentences.en: one needs to try to be perfect because you believe that people sometimes see you as being perfect when you know that to not be true about yourself.
sentences.zh: 一个人需要努力做到完美，因为你相信人们有时认为你是完美的，而你知道这对自己来说并非事实。

sentences.en: So Viola Davis was asked to play the role of Michelle Obama in a Showtime series titled The First Lady, and she described Michelle Obama as a goddess.
sentences.zh: 维奥拉·戴维斯被邀请在Showtime系列剧《第一夫人》中饰演米歇尔·奥巴马，她将米歇尔·奥巴马描述为女神。

sentences.en: I want to look at the next dimension of self-doubt and play you a clip.
sentences.zh: 我想看看自我怀疑的下一个维度，并为你播放一段片段。

sentences.en: Here is Michelle Obama talking about a question that goes through her own mind all the time.
sentences.zh: 这是米歇尔·奥巴马在谈论一个一直萦绕在她自己脑海中的问题。

sentences.en: Am I good enough?
sentences.zh: 我足够好吗？

sentences.en: That's a question that has dogged me for a good part of my life.
sentences.zh: 这个问题困扰了我大半辈子。

sentences.en: Am I good enough to have all of this?
sentences.zh: 我足够好到拥有这一切吗？

sentences.en: Am I good enough to be the First Lady of the United States?
sentences.zh: 我足够好到成为美国第一夫人吗？

sentences.en: And I think that many women and definitely many young girls of all backgrounds walk around with that question.
sentences.zh: 我认为许多女性，绝对包括许多各种背景的年轻女孩，都在带着这个问题生活。

sentences.en: I still feel that at some level I have something to prove because of the color of my skin, because of the shape of my body, because of who knows how people are judging me.
sentences.zh: 我仍然觉得在某种程度上我需要证明自己，因为我的肤色，因为我的身材，因为谁知道人们是如何评判我的。

sentences.en: So I feel like Michelle Obama is speaking to another dimension of self-doubt,
sentences.zh: 所以我感觉米歇尔·奥巴马说出了自我怀疑的另一个维度，

sentences.en: and perhaps this is similar to your own experience with self-doubt as a 29-year-old assistant professor.
sentences.zh: 也许这和你自己29岁时作为助理教授的自我怀疑经历很相似。

sentences.en: And this form of self-doubt is not that other people think too highly of you, but the fear that other people might think that you're a fraud.
sentences.zh: 而这种形式的自我怀疑不是别人对你评价太高，而是担心别人可能会认为你是个骗子。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I found myself smiling because that is the exact clip that I use in every imposter phenomenon talk that I give.
sentences.zh: 是的，我忍不住笑了，因为那正是我在每一次关于冒充者现象的演讲中使用的片段。

sentences.en: I was actually saying the words along with her as she was saying it.
sentences.zh: 当她说这些话时，我实际上也在跟着说。

sentences.en: But yeah, no, you're right.
sentences.zh: 但是的，不，你说得对。

sentences.en: In this instance, she's talking about the feelings of self-doubt that she has about herself, but that are really rooted in, I would argue,
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，她谈论的是她对自己产生的自我怀疑感，但我认为这实际上根植于，

sentences.en: societal views about people who look like her, people whom she would represent.
sentences.zh: 社会对像她这样的人，以及她所代表的人群的看法。

sentences.en: Now, you might think that one form of self-defense against these feelings is to just simply prove you're very good.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能认为对抗这些感觉的一种自我防御方式就是简单地证明你非常优秀。

sentences.en: But it turns out that doesn't always work.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明这并不总是有效。

sentences.en: The poet Maya Angelou won three Grammys for her spoken word albuMs.
sentences.zh: 诗人玛雅·安杰卢曾凭借她的口语专辑获得了三项格莱美奖。

sentences.en: She won the Pulitzer Prize for Poetry and the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
sentences.zh: 她获得了普利策诗歌奖和总统自由勋章。

sentences.en: If she had never written another word in her life, her reputation would have been secure.
sentences.zh: 如果她这辈子没再写过一个字，她的声誉也已经稳固了。

sentences.en: But you've talked about how she was also plagued by self-doubt.
sentences.zh: 但你谈到过她也曾深受自我怀疑的困扰。

sentences.en: Yeah, she talks about, you know, having published 11 books and still finding herself wondering, uh-oh, they're going to find me out.
sentences.zh: 是的，她谈到，你知道，出版了11本书后，仍然发现自己在想：噢不，他们要揭穿我了。

sentences.en: And, you know, and when I talk about her, I say, look, she is Maya freaking Angelou.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当我谈论她时，我说，看，她可是玛雅·安杰卢啊。

sentences.en: You know, she is one of the greatest portuses that we've ever, you know, experienced.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她是我们要么，你知道，经历过的最伟大的诗人之一。

sentences.en: And yet even Maya Angelou has had these feelings of being, you know, found out that she is somehow fraudulent and fooling people.
sentences.zh: 然而即使是玛雅·安杰卢也有过这种感觉，觉得自己被，你知道，揭穿了，觉得自己不知何故是欺诈者，在欺骗别人。

sentences.en: And so she is a beautiful example of someone who has achieved at the very highest level, nevertheless still feeling as though they are fraudulent.
sentences.zh: 所以她是一个美丽的例子，一个已经达到最高水平的人，却仍然觉得自己是欺诈者。

sentences.en: You know, I'm struck by the similarities between self-doubt and conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 你知道，自我怀疑和阴谋论之间的相似之处让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: Go along with me for just a second here.
sentences.zh: 跟我一起想一下，就一秒钟。

sentences.en: You know, on the surface, these are very different ideas.
sentences.zh: 你知道，表面上看，这些是非常不同的想法。

sentences.en: But one thing that unites them is that if you're plagued by self-doubt or you subscribe to a conspiracy theory, the evidence does not disabuse you of your belief.
sentences.zh: 但有一点将它们联系在一起，那就是如果你被自我怀疑所困扰，或者你相信阴谋论，证据并不能让你放弃你的信念。

sentences.en: So in the case of a conspiracy theory, you find ways to discount the evidence that contradicts the theory.
sentences.zh: 所以在阴谋论的情况下，你会找到方法去否定那些与理论相矛盾的证据。

sentences.en: And in the case of self-doubt, you know, as with Maya Angelou, no amount of past evidence that you're talented seems to convince you that your fears are not warranted.
sentences.zh: 而在自我怀疑的情况下，你知道，就像玛雅·安杰卢一样，无论过去有多少证据表明你很有才华，似乎都无法让你相信你的恐惧是没有根据的。

sentences.en: No, I mean, that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 不，我的意思是，那绝对正确。

sentences.en: In fact, it almost kind of reminds me of that social psychological concept of confirmation bias.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这几乎让我想起了社会心理学中关于确认偏误的概念。

sentences.en: You know, you are more oriented toward finding evidence that supports the contrary, that would support, you know, the idea of you not being competent, even though, again,
sentences.zh: 你知道，你更倾向于寻找支持相反观点的证据，即支持，你知道，你没有能力的观点，尽管，再说一次，

sentences.en: your accomplishments would suggest otherwise.
sentences.zh: 你的成就本该说明并非如此。

sentences.en: So I can actually see the connection.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实能看出其中的关联。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's one last dimension of self-doubt that I want to place on the table.
sentences.zh: 我想再提出最后一个自我怀疑的维度。

sentences.en: Well, the actor Tom Hanks has long been one of Hollywood's biggest stars, but like Viola Davis, he has said that he also worries that he is soon going to be found out.
sentences.zh: 演员汤姆·汉克斯长期以来一直是好莱坞最耀眼的明星之一，但和维奥拉·戴维斯一样，他也曾表示担心自己很快就会被识破。

sentences.en: No matter who we are, no matter what we've done, there comes a point where you think, how did I get here and am I going to be able to continue this?
sentences.zh: 无论我们是谁，无论我们做过什么，总会有一个时刻让你心想：我是怎么走到这一步的？我还能继续保持下去吗？

sentences.en: When are they going to discover that I am, in fact, a fraud and take everything away from me?
sentences.zh: 他们什么时候会发现我其实是个骗子，并夺走我拥有的一切？

sentences.en: It's a high wire act that we all walk, and I do this in the work that I do, because there are days when I know that three o'clock tomorrow afternoon,
sentences.zh: 我们都在走钢丝，我在自己的工作中也深有体会，因为有些时候我知道，明天下午三点，

sentences.en: I am going to have to deliver some degree of emotional goods.
sentences.zh: 我必须拿出某种程度的情感表现。

sentences.en: And if I can't do it, that means I'm going to have to fake it.
sentences.zh: 如果我做不到，那就意味着我必须伪装。

sentences.en: And if I fake it, that means they may catch me at faking it.
sentences.zh: 如果我伪装了，就意味着他们可能会发现我在伪装。

sentences.en: And if they catch me at faking it, well, then it's just doomsday.
sentences.zh: 如果他们发现我在伪装，那简直就是世界末日。

sentences.en: What strikes me in this clip, Kevin, is another dimension of self-doubt, and we've discussed this elsewhere on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 凯文，这段视频中让我印象深刻的是自我怀疑的另一个维度，我们在《隐藏的大脑》其他节目中也讨论过这一点。

sentences.en: Many of us subject ourselves to the kind of scrutiny and criticism we would never dream of aiming at other people.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人对自己施加的审视和批评，是我们绝不会对他人使用的。

sentences.en: Can you talk a moment about the harshness of our inner critic?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈我们内心那个严苛的批评者吗？

sentences.en: You know, are you yourself harder on you than you are on other people?
sentences.zh: 你对自己是否比对别人更苛刻？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's a really good question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: And I know that certainly I can see elements of that in myself, you know, when I've done something that is noteworthy and for which I should be proud of.
sentences.zh: 我确实能从自己身上看到这些影子，比如当我做了一些值得注意、本该引以为傲的事情时，

sentences.en: And nevertheless, I can still find reasons to be critical of it,
sentences.zh: 我仍然能找到理由去批评它，

sentences.en: to find reasons to not be as happy about it or excited about it or to sort of embrace it as a worthy accomplishment.
sentences.zh: 找到理由不去为此感到高兴或兴奋，或者不去把它当作一项值得的成就来欣然接受。

sentences.en: And so being our own harshest critics, that's something that I see, that I can hear in what Tom Hanks said, and certainly I can see elements of that in myself.
sentences.zh: 所以，成为自己最严厉的批评者，这是我在汤姆·汉克斯的话中看到的，也确实能在自己身上看到这些影子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's a theme that runs through many of the examples of imposter phenomenon that we have discussed.
sentences.zh: 在我们讨论过的许多冒充者现象的例子中，有一个贯穿始终的主题。

sentences.en: You know, Maya Angelou, who sort of written 11 books, thinks that she's a fraud.
sentences.zh: 比如玛雅·安杰卢，她写了11本书，却认为自己是个骗子。

sentences.en: The writer John Steinbeck is supposed to have once written something very similar.
sentences.zh: 作家约翰·斯坦贝克据说也曾写过非常类似的话。

sentences.en: He wrote, I'm not a writer.
sentences.zh: 他写道：我不是作家。

sentences.en: I've been fooling myself and other people.
sentences.zh: 我一直在欺骗自己和别人。

sentences.en: And even the physicist Albert Einstein is supposed to have once called himself an involuntary swindler.
sentences.zh: 甚至物理学家阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦据说也曾称自己为非自愿的骗子。

sentences.en: Now, on the surface, all of this seems incomprehensible.
sentences.zh: 从表面上看，这一切似乎令人费解。

sentences.en: You know, if you've written amazing books, if you've reinvented the world of physics, how can you think of yourself as a cheat and a swindler?
sentences.zh: 如果你写出了了不起的书，如果你重塑了物理学界，你怎么会认为自己是个骗子呢？

sentences.en: Why do you think it is that people who are plagued by self-doubt cannot see the brilliance that is plain for us to see when we look in from the outside?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么那些深受自我怀疑困扰的人，却看不到我们从外部观察时显而易见的才华呢？

sentences.en: You know, I think that's the million-dollar question.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是个价值百万美元的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, that's something that we are still, in many ways, trying to figure out.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这在很多方面仍是我们试图弄清楚的事情。

sentences.en: But what I will say is that if you've come from environments where you were sort of complimented on things unrelated to your intelligence.
sentences.zh: 但我会说，如果你来自那种人们只会称赞你与智力无关的事情的环境，

sentences.en: Let's say that you were someone who was very socially skilled.
sentences.zh: 假设你是一个社交能力很强的人。

sentences.en: Let's say you were someone who was very sort of, you know, athletic.
sentences.zh: 假设你是一个非常，你知道，擅长运动的人。

sentences.en: And all you ever heard from people, family and friends was about your prowess in those areas.
sentences.zh: 而你从家人和朋友那里听到的，全都是关于你在这些方面的能力。

sentences.en: But you never received feedback, you know, about your intelligence.
sentences.zh: 但你从未收到过关于你智力的反馈。

sentences.en: Then part of that can result in you internalizing this idea that, you know, maybe you're not that smart.
sentences.zh: 那么，这部分原因可能会导致你内化这样一种想法：也许你并没有那么聪明。

sentences.en: You know, maybe, you know, your talents lie elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 也许，你的天赋在别处。

sentences.en: That's part of the origins of these feelings.
sentences.zh: 这就是这些感受的部分根源。

sentences.en: Even the most successful people among us doubt their abilities from time to time.
sentences.zh: 即使是我们当中最成功的人，也时常怀疑自己的能力。

sentences.en: Self-doubt can be so powerful that it makes us feel like frauds in our own lives.
sentences.zh: 自我怀疑的力量如此强大，以至于让我们觉得自己生活中的骗子。

sentences.en: When we come back, the origins of self-doubt and what we can do about that negative voice in our heads.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨自我怀疑的根源，以及我们能对脑海中那个负面声音做些什么。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Lots of smart, talented, accomplished people harbor self-doubt.
sentences.zh: 许多聪明、有才华、有成就的人都怀有自我怀疑。

sentences.en: They worry they are frauds and imposters.
sentences.zh: 他们担心自己是骗子和冒充者。

sentences.en: Even when they have ample evidence, there is no need for such fear.
sentences.zh: 即使他们有充分的证据证明这种恐惧毫无必要。

sentences.en: At the University of Texas at Austin, psychologist Kevin Coakley studies the psychology of self-doubt and the imposter phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 在德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校，心理学家凯文·科克利研究自我怀疑和冒充者现象的心理学。

sentences.en: Kevin, the psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes first used the term imposter phenomenon in a 1978 study.
sentences.zh: 凯文，心理学家保琳·克兰斯和苏珊·伊姆斯在1978年的一项研究中首次使用了“冒充者现象”这个词。

sentences.en: They focused on high-achieving women.
sentences.zh: 她们关注的是高成就女性。

sentences.en: Can you describe that study for me and what they found?
sentences.zh: 你能为我描述一下那项研究以及她们的发现吗？

sentences.en: These were women who came from very diverse backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 这些女性来自非常多元的背景。

sentences.en: Some of them came from the world of corporate America.
sentences.zh: 有些人来自美国企业界。

sentences.en: Some of them were academics.
sentences.zh: 有些人是学者。

sentences.en: Some of them were graduate students.
sentences.zh: 有些人是研究生。

sentences.en: But what they all had in common was they were all incredibly accomplished women.
sentences.zh: 但她们的共同点是，她们都是成就斐然的女性。

sentences.en: And it was interesting because when they worked with them,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，当她们与她们合作时，

sentences.en: they kept repeatedly hearing these feelings of self-doubt in spite of the accomplishments that they had as individual women.
sentences.zh: 她们不断听到这些女性表达自我怀疑，尽管她们个人已经取得了很大成就。

sentences.en: And so it led them to theorize that this idea of the imposter phenomenon was something salient among women.
sentences.zh: 这促使她们推测，冒充者现象在女性中是一个显著的问题。

sentences.en: Because, again, this was the population they were working with.
sentences.zh: 因为，再次强调，这是她们当时研究的人群。

sentences.en: Now, the examples of people like Tom Hanks or Albert Einstein and you yourself, Kevin,
sentences.zh: 现在，像汤姆·汉克斯、阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦以及你自己，凯文，这样的例子，

sentences.en: might suggest the imposter phenomenon doesn't just affect women.
sentences.zh: 可能表明冒充者现象不仅仅影响女性。

sentences.en: Is that data to back up the anecdotes?
sentences.zh: 有数据支持这些轶事吗？

sentences.en: That's absolutely true.
sentences.zh: 绝对是真的。

sentences.en: I mean, in my own work, I have published studies where, in one study,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在我自己的工作中，我发表过研究，其中一项研究显示，

sentences.en: imposter feelings were certainly more prevalent among women than men.
sentences.zh: 冒充者感受在女性中确实比男性更普遍。

sentences.en: But in another study that I published, there was no difference between men and women.
sentences.zh: 但在我发表的另一项研究中，男性和女性之间没有差异。

sentences.en: And what we know from the accumulation of work that's been done in this area
sentences.zh: 我们从该领域积累的研究中了解到的是，

sentences.en: is that there has not been any consistent findings of women experiencing higher imposter feelings than men.
sentences.zh: 并没有任何一致的发现表明女性比男性经历更多的冒充者感受。

sentences.en: Now, that being said, and I talk about this a lot,
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我经常谈论这一点，

sentences.en: I do believe that with women that the implications of imposter feelings are a bit different than among men.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为，对于女性来说，冒充者感受的影响与男性略有不同。

sentences.en: And I point to one of the studies that I published where I was looking at factors that predict GPA.
sentences.zh: 我举我发表的一项研究为例，当时我正在研究预测平均绩点（GPA）的因素。

sentences.en: And what I found in that study was that even though there were no differences between men and women
sentences.zh: 我在那项研究中发现，尽管男性和女性之间没有差异，

sentences.en: in terms of their imposter feelings, imposter feelings had no link to GPA for men.
sentences.zh: 就冒充者感受而言，冒充者感受与男性的GPA没有关联。

sentences.en: It did not impact their grades at all.
sentences.zh: 它根本没有影响他们的成绩。

sentences.en: But for women, imposter feelings were, in fact, linked in very sort of clear ways to their GPA.
sentences.zh: 但对于女性来说，冒充者感受确实以非常明确的方式与她们的GPA相关联。

sentences.en: So you can say, on the one hand, that there were no differences in the reporting of imposter feelings
sentences.zh: 所以你可以说，一方面，两组人在报告冒充者感受方面没有差异，

sentences.en: amongst both groups, but the implications of those imposter feelings were quite different for men and women.
sentences.zh: 但这些冒充者感受对男性和女性的影响却大不相同。

sentences.en: What about racial differences here, Kevin?
sentences.zh: 凯文，种族差异方面的情况如何？

sentences.en: We've talked about several prominent black people who experience self-doubt,
sentences.zh: 我们谈到了几位经历过自我怀疑的杰出黑人，

sentences.en: but you've conducted studies looking at racial differences in self-doubt,
sentences.zh: 但你进行过研究来观察自我怀疑中的种族差异，

sentences.en: and some of the results are both revealing and surprising.
sentences.zh: 其中一些结果既有启发性又令人惊讶。

sentences.en: What do you find?
sentences.zh: 你发现了什么？

sentences.en: So in the initial study that I published, we had a very diverse sample of college students
sentences.zh: 在我发表的初步研究中，我们有一个非常多元的大学生样本，

sentences.en: consisting of Asian Americans, African Americans, and Latinx Americans.
sentences.zh: 包括亚裔美国人、非裔美国人和拉丁裔美国人。

sentences.en: And we went into the study thinking that we would see evidence of higher imposter feelings
sentences.zh: 我们进行这项研究时认为，我们会看到非裔美国人和拉丁裔美国人中，

sentences.en: among African Americans and Latinx Americans.
sentences.zh: 存在更高冒充者感受的证据。

sentences.en: And we believed that because of what we understand to be some of the ideas and beliefs
sentences.zh: 我们之所以这样认为，是因为我们理解围绕非裔美国学生和拉丁裔学生在智力方面，

sentences.en: surrounding African American students and Latinx students around intelligence
sentences.zh: 以及在他们是否有资格进入某些以白人为主的教育空间方面，存在一些观念和信念。

sentences.en: and around their deservedness to be in some predominantly white educational spaces.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，我们发现的情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: But what we found, in fact, was quite the opposite.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，在我们特定的样本中，亚裔美国学生报告的冒充者感受比非裔美国学生和拉丁裔学生更高。

sentences.en: We found that Asian American students in our particular sample reported higher feelings of imposterism
sentences.zh: 这与我们预期的发现背道而驰。

sentences.en: than both African American students and Latinx students.
sentences.zh: 我们试图从某种推测的角度来解释它，即亚裔美国学生，

sentences.en: And this was counterintuitive to what we expected to find.
sentences.zh: 不得不以某种方式应对“模范少数族裔”的神话，这加剧了这些感受。

sentences.en: And we tried to explain it somewhat speculatively on the idea that Asian American students
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这可能有点像我们之前讨论的维奥拉·戴维斯的情况，

sentences.en: have to sort of deal with that modern minority myth in ways that sort of exacerbate those feelings.
sentences.zh: 基本上是说，你知道，别人认为我很完美，但我知道我不完美。

sentences.en: I mean, it might be a little bit like what we discussed earlier about Viola Davis,
sentences.zh: 这在我的脑海中产生了一种认知失调。

sentences.en: basically saying, you know, other people think that I'm perfect, but I know I'm not perfect.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And that creates a kind of dissonance in my mind.
sentences.zh: 你刚才暗示了一点，我想我们是否可以再深入探讨一下，

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 那就是高度竞争的环境与内心产生的自我怀疑之间似乎存在联系。

sentences.en: You hinted at something a moment ago, and I'm wondering if we can explore this a little bit more,
sentences.zh: 例如，你谈到在第一份工作中走廊里走过，

sentences.en: which is there seems to be a connection between highly competitive environments
sentences.zh: 看到墙上其他教授的出版物，

sentences.en: and the internal generation of self-doubt.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这提醒你，你做得还不够多。

sentences.en: You talked, for example, about walking down the corridors at your first job
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈身处竞争环境与自我怀疑体验之间的联系吗？

sentences.en: and seeing, you know, the publications of other professors on the wall,
sentences.zh: 当你处于压力大且竞争激烈的环境中时，

sentences.en: and in some ways having this be a reminder for you that you had not done as much.
sentences.zh: 这些环境总是会成为滋生冒充者感受的温床。

sentences.en: Can you talk about the link between being in a competitive environment and the experience of self-doubt?
sentences.zh: 再次以我自己为例，你分享的关于我29岁刚从研究生院毕业就担任教授的故事，

sentences.en: When you are in environments that are stressful and that are particularly competitive,
sentences.zh: 那是一个竞争激烈的环境。

sentences.en: these always become incubators for these imposter feelings.
sentences.zh: 我认为部分原因可能只是我自己的内化，

sentences.en: Again, if I use myself as an example, you know, the story that you shared about me being a 29-year-old professor
sentences.zh: 因为并不是我的同事来找我，不断提醒我，

sentences.en: straight out of graduate school, it was a competitive environment.
sentences.zh: 你知道你身处竞争激烈的环境，你知道你必须这样做。

sentences.en: Part of it, I think, may have been just my own internalization,
sentences.zh: 不，并没有那么明确。

sentences.en: because it wasn't like I had my colleagues coming to me and constantly reminding me,
sentences.zh: 但这只是微妙的提醒，提醒你现在是一个在高效、竞争激烈的环境中的教授，

sentences.en: you know you're in a competitive environment, you know you have to do this.
sentences.zh: 他们不需要对我说什么。

sentences.en: No, it wasn't anything so explicit.
sentences.zh: 我从墙上看到的那些出版物中得到了提醒。

sentences.en: But it was just the subtle reminders that you are now a professor in a very productive, competitive environment,
sentences.zh: 你知道，你还谈到了另一个想法，关于我们如何与年轻人沟通，

sentences.en: and they didn't have to say anything to me.
sentences.zh: 特别是在教育环境中。

sentences.en: I was reminded by those publications that I saw on the walls.
sentences.zh: 如果你对一个年轻人说，我觉得你是天才，我觉得你是神童，

sentences.en: You know, you've talked about another idea about, you know, how we communicate with young people,
sentences.zh: 我觉得你很特别，在某种程度上我们可能认为是在给予对方鼓励，

sentences.en: especially in educational settings.
sentences.zh: 但我们也在给那个人施加期望。

sentences.en: If you communicate to a young person, you know, I think you're a genius, I think you're a prodigy,
sentences.zh: 所以当那个人在学习中表现不佳或在考试中表现不佳时，我的意思是，你知道，

sentences.en: I think you're special, in some ways we might think that we are communicating encouragement to the person,
sentences.zh: 他们现在正在将自己的表现与他们认为你对他们表现的看法进行比较，

sentences.en: but we're also putting expectations on that person.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得自己在退步。

sentences.en: So when that person doesn't do well in a study or doesn't do well in a test, I mean, you know,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，夸大学生对自己表现的预期，或者他们应该达到的水平，是否存在风险？

sentences.en: they're now comparing their performance with what they believe you think of their performance,
sentences.zh: 我认为存在风险。

sentences.en: and they feel like they're falling short.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当然，提供鼓励并没有错。

sentences.en: Is there a risk in some ways in over-inflating, you know, the student's sense of how good they might be
sentences.zh: 我认为所有学生都需要鼓励。

sentences.en: or how good they ought to be?
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，我确实认为人们可能会过度赞美，

sentences.en: I think there is a risk.
sentences.zh: 如果赞美的程度超过了他们对自己的认知，

sentences.en: I mean, and certainly there is nothing wrong with offering encouragement.
sentences.zh: 或者甚至超过了他们实际取得的成就，

sentences.en: I think all students need encouragement.
sentences.zh: 就会让学生陷入这种自我怀疑的挣扎中。

sentences.en: But to your point, I do think that one could go overboard with the praise
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为赞美应该与成就水平相符，

sentences.en: and set students up for struggling with these sort of feelings of self-doubt
sentences.zh: 而不是以夸张的方式进行。

sentences.en: if the level of praise exceeds what they either believe about themselves
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: or maybe even exceeds what they have actually accomplished.
sentences.zh: 所以前段时间，我们邀请了心理学家克劳德·斯蒂尔来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that the deliverance of praise should be appropriate to the level of accomplishment
sentences.zh: 那是在一期名为《他们如何看待我们》的节目中。

sentences.en: and not do so, you know, in an exaggerated manner.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了刻板印象威胁的现象。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 当你认为自己是刻板印象的目标时，这些恐惧可能成为担忧的来源，

sentences.en: So some time ago, we had the psychologist Claude Steele on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 而这种担忧会削弱你的表现。

sentences.en: It was in an episode titled How They See Us.
sentences.zh: 你在冒充者现象上的工作与克劳德在刻板印象威胁上的工作之间似乎有一些重叠。

sentences.en: And he talked about the phenomenon of stereotype threat.
sentences.zh: 我两天前刚进行过这次谈话，当时我也被问到了同样的问题。

sentences.en: When you believe you're the target of stereotypes, those fears can be a source of worry,
sentences.zh: 你的成就本该说明并非如此。

sentences.en: and that worry can undermine your performance.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实能看出其中的关联。

sentences.en: There seems to be some overlap between your work on the imposter phenomenon
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: and Claude's work on stereotype threat.
sentences.zh: 我想再提出最后一个自我怀疑的维度。

sentences.en: I was having this conversation two days ago, and I was asked this very same question.
sentences.zh: 演员汤姆·汉克斯长期以来一直是好莱坞最耀眼的明星之一，但和维奥拉·戴维斯一样，他也曾表示担心自己很快就会被识破。

sentences.en: You know, so it's something that I thought about for a while.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这其实是我思考了一段时间的问题。

sentences.en: And the way that I describe it is this.
sentences.zh: 我是这样描述它的。

sentences.en: When you think about Claude Steele's work around stereotype threat, you know,
sentences.zh: 当你想到克劳德·斯蒂尔（Claude Steele）关于“刻板印象威胁”的研究时，你知道，

sentences.en: it's this idea that individuals are aware of stereotypes that exist about once,
sentences.zh: 这是一种理念，即个人会意识到关于某种特定社会身份群体存在的刻板印象，

sentences.en: you know, a particular social identity group, whether that's based on race or gender or whatever.
sentences.zh: 无论是基于种族、性别还是其他什么因素。

sentences.en: And you don't necessarily believe the stereotypes that exist about that group,
sentences.zh: 你未必相信这些关于该群体的刻板印象，

sentences.en: but you are aware of them.
sentences.zh: 但你确实意识到了它们的存在。

sentences.en: And it's the awareness of that stereotype that ends up disrupting your performance.
sentences.zh: 正是对这种刻板印象的觉察，最终干扰了你的表现。

sentences.en: That's different from imposter feelings, because with imposter feelings,
sentences.zh: 这与“冒充者综合征”的感觉不同，因为对于冒充者综合征，

sentences.en: we talk about individuals who have internalized these beliefs that sort of lead to self-doubt.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是那些已经内化了这些信念，从而导致自我怀疑的个体。

sentences.en: You found that self-doubt can be a predictor of stress,
sentences.zh: 你发现自我怀疑可能是压力的预测指标，

sentences.en: especially for minorities in educational settings.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在教育环境中的少数群体身上。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that work?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈那项研究吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so one of the most common types of studies that you see done with the imposter phenomenon
sentences.zh: 好的，在关于冒充者现象的研究中，最常见的研究类型之一

sentences.en: is looking at two outcomes related to mental health.
sentences.zh: 是观察与心理健康相关的两个结果。

sentences.en: And, you know, I tend to look at symptoms of depression and anxiety as my outcomes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我倾向于将抑郁和焦虑症状作为我的研究结果。

sentences.en: And what we have consistently found is that individuals who experience imposter feelings
sentences.zh: 我们始终发现，那些有冒充者感觉的人，

sentences.en: have elevated symptoms of depression and have elevated symptoms of anxiety.
sentences.zh: 其抑郁和焦虑症状水平更高。

sentences.en: They are certainly linked consistently.
sentences.zh: 它们确实有着持续的关联。

sentences.en: Is it accurate to say that women and minorities in the workplace or in educational settings
sentences.zh: 说职场或教育环境中的女性和少数群体

sentences.en: might be especially prone to this correlation?
sentences.zh: 可能更容易出现这种相关性，准确吗？

sentences.en: I believe that to be the case, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我相信确实如此，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And I approach my work with the belief that for women and for BIPOC individuals,
sentences.zh: 我带着这样的信念开展工作：对于女性和有色人种（BIPOC）来说，

sentences.en: that this sort of association between mental health and imposter feelings is especially prevalent.
sentences.zh: 这种心理健康与冒充者感觉之间的关联尤为普遍。

sentences.en: Self-doubt can keep us from seeing ourselves clearly.
sentences.zh: 自我怀疑会阻碍我们清晰地认识自己。

sentences.en: It can prompt us to downplay our accomplishments and underestimate our skills.
sentences.zh: 它会促使我们淡化自己的成就，低估自己的能力。

sentences.en: It can cost us in terms of mental health and in terms of our willingness to take on new challenges.
sentences.zh: 它会让我们在心理健康和接受新挑战的意愿方面付出代价。

sentences.en: But there is a deep paradox here.
sentences.zh: 但这里存在一个深刻的悖论。

sentences.en: Even as lots of people suffer from needless self-doubt,
sentences.zh: 尽管许多人因不必要的自我怀疑而受苦，

sentences.en: many also suffer from an absence of self-doubt.
sentences.zh: 但也有许多人因缺乏自我怀疑而受苦。

sentences.en: Many people who ought to doubt themselves seem filled with blithe self-confidence.
sentences.zh: 许多本该怀疑自己的人，似乎却充满了盲目的自信。

sentences.en: When we come back, how to combat the imposter phenomenon,
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨如何对抗冒充者现象，

sentences.en: but also how to make room in our lives for the gift of self-doubt.
sentences.zh: 以及如何在我们的生活中为“自我怀疑”这种天赋留出空间。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantham）。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Even the best of us can sometimes feel we don't know what we're doing.
sentences.zh: 即使是我们中最优秀的人，有时也会觉得自己不知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: We worry that we will fall short of other people's expectations.
sentences.zh: 我们担心自己达不到别人的期望。

sentences.en: We worry that we will be called out as frauds and charlatans.
sentences.zh: 我们担心自己会被揭穿是骗子和冒牌货。

sentences.en: At the University of Texas at Austin,
sentences.zh: 在德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校，

sentences.en: psychologist Kevin Coakley studies the imposter phenomenon and what we can do about it.
sentences.zh: 心理学家凯文·科克利（Kevin Coakley）研究了冒充者现象以及我们能为此做些什么。

sentences.en: Kevin, one technique you've suggested that people use to reduce self-doubt
sentences.zh: 凯文，你建议人们用来减少自我怀疑的一种技巧

sentences.en: is to remind themselves of their accomplishments.
sentences.zh: 是提醒自己所取得的成就。

sentences.en: You say that you sometimes stalk yourself.
sentences.zh: 你说你有时会“跟踪”自己。

sentences.en: What do you mean by this?
sentences.zh: 这是什么意思？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So one of the things that happens with people who experience imposter feelings is that we
sentences.zh: 所以，对于那些有冒充者感觉的人来说，发生的一件事就是我们

sentences.en: don't acknowledge accomplishments to the extent that they should be acknowledged.
sentences.zh: 没有充分认可那些本应被认可的成就。

sentences.en: And so we sometimes just minimize them.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有时只是把它们最小化了。

sentences.en: And I somewhat half-jokingly said that I stalk myself.
sentences.zh: 我半开玩笑地说过我“跟踪”自己。

sentences.en: But what I mean is that, and I hope people out there listening don't judge me too harshly.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，我希望听众朋友们不要太严厉地评判我。

sentences.en: I go on Google almost every day, and I Google myself.
sentences.zh: 我几乎每天都会上谷歌，搜索我自己。

sentences.en: I look up my metrics surrounding my publications, how many times I've been cited, how many publications I have.
sentences.zh: 我查看关于我出版物的指标，我被引用了多少次，我有多少出版物。

sentences.en: I mean, those numbers don't change day to day.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些数字并不会每天都变。

sentences.en: But I find myself looking at them every single day because I need to remind myself that people think that you're kind of a big deal for a reason.
sentences.zh: 但我发现自己每天都在看，因为我需要提醒自己，人们认为你“了不起”是有原因的。

sentences.en: That you actually have done something of note as a scholar.
sentences.zh: 你作为一名学者确实做了一些值得注意的事情。

sentences.en: And so that's my way of just sort of reminding myself that you are deserving of the attention and the accolades that you have received.
sentences.zh: 所以，这只是我提醒自己“你配得上所获得的关注和赞誉”的一种方式。

sentences.en: And if I didn't do that, then it would be easy to sort of forget that I have accomplished this as an academic.
sentences.zh: 如果我不这样做，就很容易忘记我作为一名学者已经取得了这些成就。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I suppose it's a way you can Google yourself every day, you know, in order to stroke your vanity.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我想这是一种你可以每天谷歌自己，你知道，为了满足虚荣心的方式。

sentences.en: But I think what I'm hearing you say is actually something quite different.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我听到你说的其实是完全不同的东西。

sentences.en: It's almost like, you know, sort of a cognitive behavioral therapy intervention.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像是一种认知行为疗法的干预。

sentences.en: Because your mind is not automatically remembering all the things that you've done well, or your mind is coming up with self-doubts.
sentences.zh: 因为你的大脑不会自动记住你做得好的所有事情，或者你的大脑会产生自我怀疑。

sentences.en: Because by actually going and looking at the evidence every day, you're in some ways telling your mind, look,
sentences.zh: 因为通过每天去查看证据，你在某种程度上是在告诉你的大脑，看，

sentences.en: the belief that I have that I'm not worthy or that I'm not up to this task, this belief is untrue.
sentences.zh: 我那种“我不够好”或“我无法胜任这项任务”的信念，是不真实的。

sentences.en: So in some ways, it feels almost like a form of therapy that you've come up with on your own.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，这感觉就像是你自己发明的一种治疗方法。

sentences.en: Well, it is.
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实是。

sentences.en: And I'm so glad that you mentioned the word vanity because I fear that what I just said could come across as just someone obsessed, you know, with himself and seeing, you know,
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你提到了“虚荣”这个词，因为我担心我刚才说的话会被理解成一个沉迷于自己，你知道，只关注

sentences.en: what he's accomplished.
sentences.zh: 他所取得成就的人。

sentences.en: And it's really not that, although I can understand how it might sound that way.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此，尽管我能理解它听起来可能像那样。

sentences.en: Because in my case, I really truly sometimes find it hard to accept the fact that I am somewhat of an authority on the imposter phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 因为就我而言，我有时真的很难接受我算是冒充者现象权威的事实。

sentences.en: And so when I go and look up sort of what I've done, like, I sometimes actually forget how much work I've done in the area.
sentences.zh: 所以当我查看我所做的事情时，比如，我有时真的会忘记我在这个领域做了多少工作。

sentences.en: And I hope that people don't sort of take that to be someone who is just unduly vain about his work and read me in that way, because I'd like to think that it is not that.
sentences.zh: 我希望人们不要把它看作是一个对自己的工作过度虚荣的人，也不要那样解读我，因为我希望认为事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm not hearing that at all, Kevin.
sentences.zh: 是的，我完全没有那种感觉，凯文。

sentences.en: You know, you said a second ago that you find it hard to accept sometimes that you're an authority on the imposter phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你刚才说你有时很难接受自己是冒充者现象的权威。

sentences.en: You do see the irony here, right, Kevin, which is you're an expert on the imposter phenomenon who finds it difficult to accept that you are an expert on the imposter phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 你看到了其中的讽刺之处，对吧，凯文？那就是你是一位冒充者现象的专家，却发现很难接受自己是冒充者现象的专家。

sentences.en: I do see the irony in that statement, yes.
sentences.zh: 我确实看到了那句话里的讽刺，是的。

sentences.en: There's another idea that in some ways is a related idea, which is, you know, there are people whose accomplishments are not public.
sentences.zh: 还有另一个想法，在某种程度上是一个相关的想法，那就是，你知道，有些人他们的成就是不公开的。

sentences.en: You know, they don't have publication records.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们没有出版记录。

sentences.en: They don't have awards.
sentences.zh: 他们没有奖项。

sentences.en: But in some ways, these people can mine the same idea that you're talking about with something called a work diary.
sentences.zh: 但在某种程度上，这些人可以通过一种叫做“工作日记”的东西，来挖掘你所谈论的同一个想法。

sentences.en: Can you explain that idea to me?
sentences.zh: 你能向我解释一下那个想法吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, you know, one of the other suggestions that I give to people is to keep a work diary where you essentially document those successes that you've had in the work environment.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我给人们的另一个建议是写工作日记，你基本上记录下你在工作环境中取得的那些成功。

sentences.en: What ends up happening for people who experience imposter feelings is that it becomes very easy for us to just sort of either forget or to minimize or marginalize those things that we've done well during the course of a day,
sentences.zh: 对于那些有冒充者感觉的人来说，最终发生的事情是，我们很容易忘记、最小化或边缘化那些我们在一天中、

sentences.en: during the course of a week.
sentences.zh: 在一周中做得好的事情。

sentences.en: And so sometimes we have to be intentional about documenting those little successes that in the aggregate, you know, are pretty impressive.
sentences.zh: 所以有时我们必须有意识地记录下那些小小的成功，这些成功加在一起，你知道，是相当令人印象深刻的。

sentences.en: So, Kevin, we've talked about ways that individuals can manage their self-doubt.
sentences.zh: 那么，凯文，我们已经讨论了个人管理自我怀疑的方法。

sentences.en: Are there things that organizations can do that can also reduce self-doubt?
sentences.zh: 组织是否也能做些什么来减少自我怀疑？

sentences.en: Yes, there certainly are things that organizations can do.
sentences.zh: 是的，组织当然可以做一些事情。

sentences.en: And the example that I like to give involves individuals who are managers, you know, or supervisors.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢举的例子涉及那些经理，你知道，或者主管。

sentences.en: And what you can do as a manager or a supervisor to really sort of mitigate these sort of feelings of imposterism amongst your subordinates is being transparent in your own vulnerabilities and to be open in sharing this with their employees.
sentences.zh: 作为经理或主管，为了真正减轻下属这种冒充者感觉，你可以做的是在自己的脆弱性上保持透明，并乐于与员工分享这些。

sentences.en: It really helps individuals who are afraid to own up or to sort of say, I've made a mistake.
sentences.zh: 这真的能帮助那些害怕承认或说“我犯了一个错误”的人。

sentences.en: It makes them feel like, you know what, if my manager or my supervisor can talk openly about making a mistake, then it's OK for me to make a mistake.
sentences.zh: 这让他们觉得，你知道吗，如果我的经理或主管能公开谈论犯错，那么我犯错也没关系。

sentences.en: And I don't have to be perfect.
sentences.zh: 我不必追求完美。

sentences.en: And I think that that goes a long way towards helping to assuage any feelings of imposterism that an individual might be experiencing.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对于缓解个人可能经历的任何冒充者感觉大有裨益。

sentences.en: Researchers have also looked at ways to dismantle the imposter phenomenon in schools.
sentences.zh: 研究人员也研究了在学校消除冒充者现象的方法。

sentences.en: At Stanford University, Greg Walton looked at the problems that incoming freshmen were facing.
sentences.zh: 在斯坦福大学，格雷格·沃尔顿（Greg Walton）研究了新生面临的问题。

sentences.en: And he found that when they experienced setbacks, many of them drew global conclusions like, you know, I don't belong here or I don't deserve to be here.
sentences.zh: 他发现，当他们遇到挫折时，许多人会得出全局性的结论，比如，你知道，“我不属于这里”或“我不配待在这里”。

sentences.en: And he felt like blacks were especially likely to feel like they were frauds.
sentences.zh: 他觉得黑人学生特别容易觉得自己是骗子。

sentences.en: And so he set up an intervention that helped black students see setbacks in the proper perspective.
sentences.zh: 于是他建立了一个干预措施，帮助黑人学生以正确的视角看待挫折。

sentences.en: So a bad test result or a bad interaction with a professor didn't mean that they were frauds.
sentences.zh: 所以，糟糕的考试成绩或与教授的不愉快互动并不意味着他们是骗子。

sentences.en: It didn't mean they were imposters.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着他们是冒充者。

sentences.en: It just meant that they were having, you know, a bad day or a bad week.
sentences.zh: 这只是意味着他们，你知道，度过了糟糕的一天或一周。

sentences.en: Here's a clip of Greg describing the effects of his intervention.
sentences.zh: 这是一段格雷格描述他干预措施效果的片段。

sentences.en: What the intervention did was it prevented students from feeling that they didn't belong in general when they had negative experiences.
sentences.zh: 这种干预措施的作用是，防止学生在经历负面体验时产生“我不属于这里”的普遍感觉。

sentences.en: You can then imagine how, if you're feeling less vulnerable to threats, you are better able to connect with other people, to peers, to teachers,
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，如果你感觉对威胁的脆弱性降低了，你就更能与他人、同龄人、老师建立联系，

sentences.en: and build the kinds of relationships that actually sustain performance over a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 并建立起那种能长期维持表现的关系。

sentences.en: Kevin, I'm wondering if you can weigh in on this.
sentences.zh: 凯文，我想知道你对此有什么看法。

sentences.en: Is one solution to self-doubt in some ways not, you know, blowing things out of proportion, blowing setbacks out of proportion?
sentences.zh: 解决自我怀疑的一个方案，在某种程度上是不是，你知道，不要把事情夸大，不要把挫折夸大？

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个说法。

sentences.en: And thank you for sharing that study.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你分享那项研究。

sentences.en: You know, as a counseling psychologist,
sentences.zh: 你知道，作为一名咨询心理学家，

sentences.en: I would sort of refer to that as almost like I'm simply reframing it and not sort of internalizing it as being indicative of a trait about yourself.
sentences.zh: 我会把它称为——我只是在重构它，而不是把它内化为关于你自身的一种特质。

sentences.en: People aren't perfect.
sentences.zh: 人无完人。

sentences.en: And we have to sort of get beyond this idea that making mistakes is somehow indicative of you being not smart, not competent, not belonging.
sentences.zh: 我们必须超越这种想法，即犯错在某种程度上意味着你不聪明、不称职、不属于这里。

sentences.en: The most accomplished people in the world have all experienced failure at some point.
sentences.zh: 世界上最有成就的人都在某个时刻经历过失败。

sentences.en: And so we need to sort of help students in particular understand that when you fail a test, and I could have benefited from this when I was a student,
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要帮助学生，特别是让他们明白，当你考试不及格时——如果我还是学生时能得到这种帮助就好了——

sentences.en: it would have been so helpful if I would have had a professor who would have pulled me to the side and to help me sort of manage the feelings that I was having around my initial sort of early poor performance.
sentences.zh: 如果有一位教授能把我拉到一边，帮助我处理我围绕早期糟糕表现所产生的感受，那将非常有帮助。

sentences.en: It's okay.
sentences.zh: 没关系的。

sentences.en: It's okay.
sentences.zh: 没关系的。

sentences.en: Just don't let it be defining of who you are and what your potentiality is.
sentences.zh: 只是不要让它定义你是谁以及你的潜力是什么。

sentences.en: And I think we don't have enough of that taking place in schools.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们在学校里做得还不够。

sentences.en: You know, Kevin, we started this conversation talking about some of your own insecurities and self-doubts.
sentences.zh: 你知道，凯文，我们开始这次谈话时谈到了你自身的一些不安全感和自我怀疑。

sentences.en: When you are plagued by self-doubt, even today, you say that you have a go-to solution and it involves effort.
sentences.zh: 当你被自我怀疑困扰时，即使在今天，你说你有一个首选的解决方案，而且它涉及努力。

sentences.en: Can you explain what you do maybe with a specific example?
sentences.zh: 你能用一个具体的例子解释一下你做什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, and I'll start off by, you know, going back to Michelle Obama.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我先从，你知道，回到米歇尔·奥巴马（Michelle Obama）说起。

sentences.en: Michelle Obama says that what she does is essentially, you know, she works hard.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔·奥巴马说她所做的基本上是，你知道，她努力工作。

sentences.en: She works harder.
sentences.zh: 她更加努力地工作。

sentences.en: So whenever I doubted myself, I just told myself, let me put my head down and do the work.
sentences.zh: 所以每当我怀疑自己时，我就告诉自己，让我埋头苦干，把工作做好。

sentences.en: And I would let my work speak for itself.
sentences.zh: 我会让我的工作说明一切。

sentences.en: And I still find that I do that.
sentences.zh: 我发现我至今仍这样做。

sentences.en: And I really identify with that because that has been the way that I try to address my feelings of imposterism.
sentences.zh: 我真的很有共鸣，因为这就是我尝试解决冒充者感觉的方式。

sentences.en: When I think about those early days of my being an assistant professor, I would work late in the evenings.
sentences.zh: 当我想到我刚做助理教授的那段日子，我会在晚上工作到很晚。

sentences.en: I found myself working on the weekends because I needed to prove to people and I think probably most importantly to myself that I belong.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己在周末也在工作，因为我需要向人们证明，而且我认为最重要的是向我自己证明，我属于这里。

sentences.en: And so I just I worked incessantly.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是，我不断地工作。

sentences.en: Now, I will say that hard work without having a way to sort of balance that with play is not necessarily a good thing.
sentences.zh: 现在，我要说的是，没有平衡工作与娱乐的方式的努力工作，并不一定是一件好事。

sentences.en: But but what I will say is, is that that hard work oftentimes, you know,
sentences.zh: 但我会说的是，那种努力工作往往，你知道，

sentences.en: can result in achievement and accomplishment in ways that you would hope would help mitigate whatever feelings of imposterism you might be experiencing.
sentences.zh: 可以带来成就和成果，以你希望的方式帮助减轻你可能正在经历的任何冒充者感觉。

sentences.en: Do you still do that even today, Kevin?
sentences.zh: 凯文，即使在今天，你还会这样做吗？

sentences.en: Is this your response when someone asks you to give a talk or you have to make a big presentation and you're and you're plagued with self-doubt?
sentences.zh: 当有人请你演讲，或者你必须做一个重要的演示，而你被自我怀疑困扰时，这是你的反应吗？

sentences.en: Do you respond to that by doubling down on the amount of time you're spending in preparation?
sentences.zh: 你是否通过加倍投入准备时间来应对？

sentences.en: You know, there there are elements of that when Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes, and I think it was really Pauline Clance.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这其中有这方面的因素，当宝琳·克兰斯（Pauline Clance）和苏珊·艾姆斯（Suzanne Imes）——我想主要是宝琳·克兰斯——

sentences.en: She she talked about the imposter cycle and she she talked about these two pathways that that people take, you know,
sentences.zh: 她谈到了冒充者循环，她谈到了人们采取的这两条路径，你知道，

sentences.en: the pathway of over preparedness and the pathway of procrastination.
sentences.zh: 过度准备的路径和拖延的路径。

sentences.en: And I'm the person who goes through the pathway of over preparedness.
sentences.zh: 而我就是那个走“过度准备”路径的人。

sentences.en: And for me, what that means is, you know, when I am giving a talk on the imposter phenomenon, a talk that I have given more times than I can count,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这意味着，你知道，当我正在做一个关于冒充者现象的演讲时，一个我已经讲过无数次的演讲，

sentences.en: I still prepare as though I have never given the talk before.
sentences.zh: 我仍然像从未做过这个演讲一样去准备。

sentences.en: And it's because I want to make sure that when I give the talk that people hear me and experience me as being an expert and leave no doubt in their mind that I know what I'm talking about.
sentences.zh: 这是因为我想确保当我演讲时，人们能听进去，并感受到我是专家，让他们心中毫无疑问地认为我所言非虚。

sentences.en: So, yeah, there are still elements of that in in me even today.
sentences.zh: 所以，没错，即使在今天，我身上依然保留着那些特质。

sentences.en: You know, I'm struck by what you just said, Kevin, because when I when I listen to that clip of Viola Davis talk about, you know, feeling like an imposter,
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，凯文，你刚才说的话让我深受触动，因为当我听到维奥拉·戴维斯谈论那种“冒充者综合征”的感觉时，

sentences.en: I didn't play the whole clip for you.
sentences.zh: 我并没有给你播放完整的片段。

sentences.en: She goes on to say something really interesting, which is, you know, she doesn't say, you know, woe is me.
sentences.zh: 她接着说了一些非常有趣的话，她并没有说“我真可怜”。

sentences.en: I have all these insecurities.
sentences.zh: 我有这么多不安全感。

sentences.en: Feel sorry for me.
sentences.zh: 请同情我吧。

sentences.en: She talks about how she uses her insecurities as a driver, as motivation.
sentences.zh: 她谈到自己是如何将这些不安全感转化为动力，作为激励自己的源泉。

sentences.en: Anybody who even wants to be great has that anybody, any filmmaker, any writer, any actor.
sentences.zh: 任何想要变得卓越的人，无论是电影制作人、作家还是演员，都有这种感觉。

sentences.en: But what it does on a healthy level, it keeps you humble and it keeps you working.
sentences.zh: 但在健康的层面上，它能让你保持谦逊，并让你不断努力工作。

sentences.en: I'm hearing almost exactly what you said to me a second ago, Kevin, which is that in some ways, you know,
sentences.zh: 我听到的几乎和你刚才对我说的如出一辙，凯文，也就是说，在某种程度上，

sentences.en: not believing the good press about you turns out to actually be a powerful motivator for you to actually put your nose to the grindstone, if you will.
sentences.zh: 不轻信那些关于你的溢美之词，反而成了你脚踏实地、努力工作的强大动力。

sentences.en: You know, Viola Davis is so insightful.
sentences.zh: 你知道，维奥拉·戴维斯非常有洞察力。

sentences.en: I mean, and she is absolutely correct.
sentences.zh: 我是说，她完全正确。

sentences.en: And I would say that what she has said definitely applies to me.
sentences.zh: 我想说，她所说的话绝对适用于我。

sentences.en: I think humility is very important.
sentences.zh: 我认为谦逊非常重要。

sentences.en: And if I ever got to the point where I lost my humility, I would be brought back to Earth by my my wife, who is also an academic.
sentences.zh: 如果我有一天失去了谦逊，我的妻子——她也是一位学者——会把我拉回现实。

sentences.en: She would quickly revive me of, I knew you win.
sentences.zh: 她会很快让我清醒过来，提醒我别得意忘形。

sentences.en: And I think that's necessary because I never want to get to the point where I have forgotten that I was that that young assistant professor with one publication and full of self-doubts starting my career.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很有必要，因为我永远不想忘记自己曾经也是那个只有一篇论文、充满自我怀疑、刚开启职业生涯的年轻助理教授。

sentences.en: I never want to forget that person because that person is still inside of me.
sentences.zh: 我永远不想忘记那个人，因为那个人依然活在我的内心深处。

sentences.en: And it continues to fuel me and and motivate me to being the best academic that I can be.
sentences.zh: 它持续地激励着我，鞭策我成为我所能成为的最优秀的学者。

sentences.en: I'm wondering in some ways, Kevin, whether this might be at least a partial solution to the paradox we identified in the first part of our conversation.
sentences.zh: 凯文，我在想，这是否在某种程度上是我们对话第一部分中提到的那个悖论的部分解决方案？

sentences.en: You know, we looked at how many brilliant people like Maya Angelou or Albert Einstein have been plagued by self-doubt.
sentences.zh: 我们观察到，许多像玛雅·安杰卢或阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦这样才华横溢的人，都深受自我怀疑的困扰。

sentences.en: From the outside, that looks bizarre.
sentences.zh: 从外人的角度看，这显得很奇怪。

sentences.en: But is it possible that we actually have mixed up cause and effect?
sentences.zh: 但有没有可能我们搞反了因果关系？

sentences.en: They are not plagued by self-doubt in spite of being great.
sentences.zh: 他们并非因为伟大而受到自我怀疑的困扰。

sentences.en: Their greatness is being driven, at least in part, by the fuel of self-doubt.
sentences.zh: 他们的伟大，至少在某种程度上，正是由自我怀疑这种燃料所驱动的。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: No, I think you're right.
sentences.zh: 不，我想你是对的。

sentences.en: I think that that is very much a possibility that their self-doubt in part, you know, fuels their greatness.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很有可能，他们的自我怀疑在一定程度上助推了他们的伟大。

sentences.en: I think there's an argument to be made for that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个观点是站得住脚的。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if it might be helpful almost for a moment to think about what would happen if we lived in a world without self-doubt.
sentences.zh: 我在想，如果能花点时间思考一下，如果我们生活在一个没有自我怀疑的世界里会怎样，这是否会有所帮助？

sentences.en: You know, I'm thinking back to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我在回想美国在2003年

sentences.en: invasion of Iraq in 2003.
sentences.zh: 入侵伊拉克的那件事。

sentences.en: You know, the Bush administration said the invasion was necessary because Iraq was developing weapons of mass destruction.
sentences.zh: 布什政府当时称入侵是必要的，因为伊拉克正在研制大规模杀伤性武器。

sentences.en: And at one press conference, Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld was told that the Iraqi government had denied possessing weapons of mass destruction.
sentences.zh: 在一次新闻发布会上，国防部长唐纳德·拉姆斯菲尔德被告知，伊拉克政府否认拥有大规模杀伤性武器。

sentences.en: Let me play a clip of that press conference.
sentences.zh: 让我播放一下那场新闻发布会的片段。

sentences.en: What do you make of the statement made by the Iraqi government yesterday that Iraq has no weapons of mass destruction and is not developing?
sentences.zh: 你如何看待伊拉克政府昨天发表的声明，即伊拉克没有大规模杀伤性武器，也没有在研制这些武器？

sentences.en: They're lying.
sentences.zh: 他们在撒谎。

sentences.en: No, they have them and they continue to develop them and they've weaponized chemical weapons.
sentences.zh: 不，他们拥有这些武器，并且还在继续研制，他们已经将化学武器武器化了。

sentences.en: And as we know that, they've had an active program to develop nuclear weapons.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所知，他们有一个积极的核武器研制计划。

sentences.en: It's also clear that they are actively developing biological weapons.
sentences.zh: 同样清楚的是，他们正在积极研制生物武器。

sentences.en: So as we know, Kevin, Iraq did not possess those weapons.
sentences.zh: 所以正如我们所知，凯文，伊拉克并没有那些武器。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering if you can talk a moment about what seems like this paradox.
sentences.zh: 我想请你谈谈这个看似悖论的问题。

sentences.en: How is it that some of us are plagued with self-doubt while others could use a little more self-doubt?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们有些人深受自我怀疑的困扰，而另一些人却需要多一点自我怀疑？

sentences.en: You know, that is a very good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: And it immediately sort of reminded me of the saying, you know, pride falleth before the man.
sentences.zh: 它立刻让我想起了那句谚语：“骄兵必败”。

sentences.en: And I think about what happens when hubris gets in the way of our ability to make reasoned and reasonable sort of decisions.
sentences.zh: 我想到当傲慢阻碍我们做出理性和合理的决策时会发生什么。

sentences.en: And I think that having a bit of self-doubt could save us from really bad situations such as unnecessary wars, among other things.
sentences.zh: 我认为拥有一点自我怀疑可以让我们免于陷入非常糟糕的境地，比如不必要的战争等等。

sentences.en: And so it certainly would have been nice if Rumsfeld had exhibited a bit more humility than his response indicated.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果拉姆斯菲尔德当时能表现出比他回应中更多的谦逊，那肯定会更好。

sentences.en: But no, I mean, I think I like the way that you sort of connected that to real-world implications.
sentences.zh: 没错，我很喜欢你把它与现实世界的影响联系起来的方式。

sentences.en: And to me, it does sort of go back to this idea of people not feeling so overly confident in themselves in ways that are unhelpful and are unhealthy.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这确实回到了那个观点：人们不应该在那些无益且不健康的方面对自己过度自信。

sentences.en: I can't say enough about how in my own life the need to be humble, to even have feelings of self-doubt have been helpful.
sentences.zh: 我怎么强调谦逊的必要性都不为过，即使是自我怀疑的感觉，在我的生活中也曾起到过帮助。

sentences.en: Because if I did not have those feelings of self-doubt, then I think that that would, one, make me probably an unbearable person and not very pleasant to be around.
sentences.zh: 因为如果我没有那种自我怀疑的感觉，首先，我可能会变得难以相处，让人感到厌烦。

sentences.en: But it also has kept me, I think, hungry to continue to work hard to prove myself.
sentences.zh: 但它也让我保持渴望，不断努力工作来证明自己。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, when you get to the point where you stop wanting to prove yourself and you're no longer hungry and motivated, I don't think that's a very good place to be.
sentences.zh: 我认为，当你不再想证明自己，不再有渴望和动力时，那并不是一个好的状态。

sentences.en: So I feel we're in very deep waters here, Kevin.
sentences.zh: 凯文，我觉得我们现在讨论的话题非常深刻。

sentences.en: I mean, on the one hand, we've seen how experiencing discrimination, being an outsider, this can increase the risk that you will experience the imposter phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 一方面，我们看到经历歧视、作为局外人，这会增加你产生“冒充者综合征”的风险。

sentences.en: And that's clearly unfair.
sentences.zh: 这显然是不公平的。

sentences.en: You know, feelings of self-doubt can cause people to drop out of school, cause them to quit professions that they would be great at.
sentences.zh: 你知道，自我怀疑的感觉会导致人们辍学，导致他们放弃本可以大有作为的职业。

sentences.en: On the other hand, lots of people also turn their insecurity into a superpower like yourself, and they use it as fuel.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，许多人也像你一样，将不安全感转化为一种超能力，并将其作为燃料。

sentences.en: And a lack of self-doubt, especially when you wield great power, can produce terrible harm.
sentences.zh: 而缺乏自我怀疑，尤其是在你掌握巨大权力时，可能会造成可怕的伤害。

sentences.en: So I guess I'm left wondering, is self-doubt a bad thing or a good thing?
sentences.zh: 所以我不得不思考，自我怀疑究竟是坏事还是好事？

sentences.en: Self-doubt can be a good thing when it is used as a source of motivation to achieve, to excel.
sentences.zh: 当自我怀疑被用作实现目标、追求卓越的动力来源时，它可以是一件好事。

sentences.en: But it can come at great cost to one's mental health and to one's physical health.
sentences.zh: 但它也可能以牺牲心理健康和身体健康为沉重代价。

sentences.en: And so, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，

sentences.en: the challenge then is to sort of figure out how to use one's self-doubt in ways that don't result in there being any sort of compromises to your mental health or physical health.
sentences.zh: 挑战在于如何找到一种方法，利用自我怀疑，同时又不损害自己的心理或身体健康。

sentences.en: And so, you know, the example that I, you know, sometimes share with people, you know, comes from African-American psychology, where we talk about the John Henryism hypothesis.
sentences.zh: 我有时会和人们分享一个例子，它来自非裔美国人心理学，我们称之为“约翰·亨利主义”假说。

sentences.en: And this comes from a story, folklore story of an individual named John Henry, who was a steel driver, who was essentially put in a situation where he was competing against,
sentences.zh: 这个故事源于一个民间传说，主角叫约翰·亨利，他是一名钢钎工，他被置于一种必须与机器竞争的境地，

sentences.en: you know, a machine to perform.
sentences.zh: 去完成工作。

sentences.en: And the short version of the story is, is that he wanted to prove that he could outperform this machine.
sentences.zh: 故事的简短版本是，他想证明自己能胜过那台机器。

sentences.en: Well, he worked and he worked and he worked and he worked and he eventually did beat the machine.
sentences.zh: 他不停地工作，最终他确实打败了机器。

sentences.en: And so his achievement was quite high because he won.
sentences.zh: 他的成就感很高，因为他赢了。

sentences.en: But it came at the cost of his life because he ended up dying from the exertion of effort that he gave.
sentences.zh: 但代价是他的生命，因为他最终因过度劳累而死。

sentences.en: So we want to be careful that we don't achieve such incredible feats of accomplishment that ultimately result in harming our mental health and our physical health.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要小心，不要为了取得惊人的成就，最终却损害了我们的心理和身体健康。

sentences.en: I'm going to be a steel driving man.
sentences.zh: 我要成为一名钢钎工。

sentences.en: In your own life, Kevin, have you come to think of self-doubt as a friend or as an enemy?
sentences.zh: 凯文，在你自己的生活中，你把自我怀疑看作是朋友还是敌人？

sentences.en: Oh, my goodness.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: That's a you ask really difficult questions.
sentences.zh: 你问的问题真的很难。

sentences.en: Self-doubt, I think for me, I would say probably has been more of a friend than an enemy for me.
sentences.zh: 对于我来说，我想自我怀疑可能更像是一个朋友，而不是敌人。

sentences.en: I do try to take care of myself.
sentences.zh: 我确实努力照顾好自己。

sentences.en: I work out.
sentences.zh: 我锻炼身体。

sentences.en: I try to be, you know, healthy.
sentences.zh: 我努力保持健康。

sentences.en: But I have certainly used self-doubt in ways as a constant source of motivation to make sure that I am not complacent.
sentences.zh: 但我确实利用自我怀疑作为一种持续的动力，确保自己不会自满。

sentences.en: So I am aware of the things that I need to do to provide this sort of balance and that I continue to strive to be the best academic that I can be.
sentences.zh: 所以我清楚自己需要做什么来保持这种平衡，并继续努力成为我所能成为的最优秀的学者。

sentences.en: So I think in my case, it has probably been more of a friend than an enemy.
sentences.zh: 所以我想在我的情况下，它可能更像是一个朋友，而不是敌人。

sentences.en: Kevin Coakley is a psychologist at the University of Texas at Austin.
sentences.zh: 凯文·科克利是德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校的心理学家。

sentences.en: He is the author of The Myth of Black Anti-Intellectualism, A True Psychology of African-American Students.
sentences.zh: 他是《黑人反智主义的神话：非裔美国学生的真实心理学》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Kevin, thank you for joining me today on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 凯文，感谢你今天参加《Hidden Brain》节目。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

sentences.zh: 我们本周的无名英雄是胡安娜·梅洛。

sentences.zh: 胡安娜是一位平面设计师，她在2015年创作了《Hidden Brain》的标志。

sentences.zh: 她有着惊人的审美眼光，当你看到《我的无名英雄》的标志时就会明白。
